stem.es: Dos puntos están en (−6, −2) y (5, −2). Explica cómo hallar la distancia entre ellos y por qué se suma en lugar de restar.

criteria.en: Notes the y-coordinates match, so the segment is horizontal
criteria.es: Nota que las coordenadas y coinciden, así que el segmento es horizontal

criteria.en: Says the points are on opposite sides of the y-axis
criteria.es: Dice que los puntos están en lados opuestos del eje y

criteria.en: Adds 6 and 5 to get 11 units
criteria.es: Suma 6 y 5 y obtiene 11 unidades

sample.en: The y-coordinates are both −2, so I look at the x-coordinates. −6 is 6 units left of the y-axis and 5 is 5 units right. They are on opposite sides, so I add: 6 + 5 = 11 units.
sample.es: Ambas coordenadas y son −2, así que miro las coordenadas x. −6 está 6 unidades a la izquierda del eje y y 5 está 5 a la derecha. Están en lados opuestos, así que sumo: 6 + 5 = 11 unidades.

hints.en: Which coordinate is the same for both points?
Where is each x-coordinate compared with the y-axis?
Distances from 0 on opposite sides combine.

steps: Same y, so the distance depends on x.
solution.es: |−6| + |5| = 11 unidades porque están en lados opuestos del eje y.

objective: Use a negative integer to represent a quantity below a reference point.

stem.en: A diver swims 12 meters below sea level. Which integer shows her position compared with sea level?
stem.es: Una buzo nada a 12 metros bajo el nivel del mar. ¿Qué entero muestra su posición respecto al nivel del mar?

choices.why: That is much too close to sea level. She is 12 whole meters down.
0 is sea level itself. She is 12 meters away from it.
A positive number would mean above sea level. She is below sea level.

hints.en: Sea level is the reference point, 0.
Below the reference point is the negative side.
The distance below tells the size of the number.

solution.es: Doce metros bajo el nivel del mar se representan con −12.

objective: Explain why dividing by a fraction less than 1 gives a larger quotient.

stem.en: Marco says that dividing 6 by 1/2 must give an answer smaller than 6, because dividing makes numbers smaller. Explain why Marco is not right.
stem.es: Marco dice que dividir 6 entre 1/2 debe dar una respuesta menor que 6, porque dividir hace los números más pequeños. Explica por qué Marco no tiene razón.

criteria.en: Says 6 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves fit in 6
criteria.es: Dice que 6 ÷ 1/2 pregunta cuántas mitades caben en 6

criteria.en: Finds that each whole has 2 halves, so the answer is 12
criteria.es: Halla que cada entero tiene 2 mitades, así que la respuesta es 12

criteria.en: Concludes 12 is greater than 6
criteria.es: Concluye que 12 es mayor que 6

sample.en: 6 ÷ 1/2 asks how many halves are in 6. Each whole has 2 halves, so there are 6 × 2 = 12 halves. 12 is bigger than 6, so dividing by a fraction less than 1 can make a bigger number.
sample.es: 6 ÷ 1/2 pregunta cuántas mitades hay en 6. Cada entero tiene 2 mitades, así que hay 6 × 2 = 12 mitades. 12 es mayor que 6, por lo que dividir entre una fracción menor que 1 puede dar un número mayor.

hints.en: Think of dividing as asking how many groups fit.
How many halves fit in one whole?
Compare your answer with 6.

steps: Each whole has 2 halves, so 6 wholes have 12 halves.
solution.es: 6 ÷ 1/2 = 12, que es mayor que 6, porque en cada entero caben 2 mitades.

objective: Divide a four-digit number by a two-digit number with the standard algorithm.

hints.en: Start with the first digits that make a number at least as large as 12.
12 goes into 43 three times; bring down the next digit and keep going.
Check your quotient by multiplying it by 12.

steps: 12 into 43 is 3 (36), remainder 7; bring down 6 to make 76.
12 into 76 is 6 (72), remainder 4; bring down 8 to make 48; 12 into 48 is 4. The quotient is 364.
solution.es: El cociente es 364 porque 12 × 364 = 4,368.

objective: Divide by a two-digit divisor when estimating the next digit is needed.

stem.en: Divide: 9,576 ÷ 38. What is the quotient?
stem.es: Divide: 9,576 ÷ 38. ¿Cuál es el cociente?

hints.en: Estimate by rounding 38 to 40.
38 goes into 95 two times.
Multiply and subtract, bring down the next digit, and estimate again.

steps: 38 into 95 is 2 (76), remainder 19; bring down 7 to make 197.
38 into 197 is 5 (190), remainder 7; bring down 6 to make 76; 38 into 76 is 2. The quotient is 252.

objective: Use place value to choose a reasonable quotient.

stem.en: Without dividing the long way, which is the quotient of 4,200 ÷ 35?
stem.es: Sin dividir por el método largo, ¿cuál es el cociente de 4,200 ÷ 35?

choices.why: 4,200 ÷ 35 is much more than 12. 35 × 12 is only 420.
35 × 125 = 4,375, which is more than 4,200.
35 × 1,200 is 42,000, ten times too big.

hints.en: Think of 4,200 as 420 tens.
42 ÷ 35 is a little more than 1; adjust for place value.
Check the choices by multiplying by 35.

objective: Solve a measurement division problem with mixed numbers.

stem.en: A baker has 5 1/4 pounds of flour. Each batch of muffins uses 3/4 pound. How many batches can the baker make?
stem.es: Un panadero tiene 5 1/4 libras de harina. Cada tanda de panecillos usa 3/4 de libra. ¿Cuántas tandas puede hacer el panadero?

criteria.en: Writes 5 1/4 as 21/4
criteria.es: Escribe 5 1/4 como 21/4

criteria.en: Divides 21/4 by 3/4
criteria.es: Divide 21/4 entre 3/4

criteria.en: Gets 7 batches
criteria.es: Obtiene 7 tandas

hints.en: Change the mixed number to an improper fraction first.
Both fractions are fourths, so count how many 3 fourths fit in the fourths you have.
Divide the number of fourths by 3.

objective: Identify points a given distance from the x-axis using absolute value.

stem.en: Select ALL the points that are exactly 4 units from the x-axis.
stem.es: Selecciona TODOS los puntos que están exactamente a 4 unidades del eje x.

choices.why: The distance from the x-axis is the size of the y-coordinate, which is 1. The 4 is the x-coordinate.
The distance from the x-axis is |6| = 6, not 4.

hints.en: The distance from the x-axis depends on only one coordinate.
Use the absolute value of the y-coordinate.
Check |y| for each point.

solution.es: La distancia al eje x es |y|; (3, 4), (−2, −4) y (0, −4) tienen |y| = 4.

objective: Find the greatest common factor of two numbers.

stem.en: What is the greatest common factor of 36 and 48?
stem.es: ¿Cuál es el máximo común divisor de 36 y 48?

hints.en: List the factors of each number.
Find the factors that appear in both lists.
Choose the largest one on both lists.

solution.es: El mayor factor común de 36 y 48 es 12.

objective: Rewrite a sum of two whole numbers as the GCF times a sum.

stem.en: Use the greatest common factor to write 42 + 56 as a product of the GCF and a sum of two numbers with no common factor other than 1.
stem.es: Usa el máximo común divisor para escribir 42 + 56 como el producto del MCD y una suma de dos números sin otro factor común más que 1.

hints.en: First find the greatest common factor of 42 and 56.
Divide each number by the GCF to get the numbers inside the parentheses.
Check by distributing the GCF over the sum.

solution.es: El MCD de 42 y 56 es 14, entonces 42 + 56 = 14(3 + 4).

objective: Identify which pair of numbers has a given greatest common factor.

stem.en: Which pair of numbers has a greatest common factor of 6?
stem.es: ¿Qué pareja de números tiene un máximo común divisor de 6?

choices.why: The greatest common factor of 8 and 12 is 4, not 6.
The greatest common factor of 15 and 20 is 5.
9 and 14 share no factor except 1.

hints.en: Find the greatest common factor of each pair.
List the factors of both numbers in a pair.
6 must divide both numbers and nothing larger can.

steps: The other pairs have GCFs of 4, 5 and 1.
solution.es: El MCD de 12 y 18 es 6; los otros pares tienen MCD de 4, 5 y 1.

objective: Use the greatest common factor to make equal groups with nothing left over.

stem.en: A teacher has 30 pencils and 45 erasers. She wants to make identical supply kits using all of them with none left over. What is the greatest number of kits she can make?
stem.es: Una maestra tiene 30 lápices y 45 borradores. Quiere armar kits de útiles idénticos usando todo, sin que sobre nada. ¿Cuál es el mayor número de kits que puede armar?

criteria.es: Ve que el número de kits debe dividir 30 y 45

criteria.en: Finds the greatest common factor is 15
criteria.es: Halla que el máximo común divisor es 15

sample.en: The number of kits must be a factor of both 30 and 45. The greatest common factor is 15, so she can make 15 kits (2 pencils and 3 erasers each).
sample.es: El número de kits debe ser un factor de 30 y de 45. El máximo común divisor es 15, así que puede armar 15 kits (2 lápices y 3 borradores cada uno).

hints.en: The number of kits must divide evenly into both amounts.
Look for the largest number that is a factor of both.
Check by dividing 30 and 45 by your answer.

solution.es: El mayor factor común de 30 y 45 es 15 kits.

objective: Compare negative rational numbers to find the greatest.

stem.en: Which of these numbers is the greatest?
stem.es: ¿Cuál de estos números es el mayor?

choices.why: −5 is the farthest left on the number line, so it is the least, not the greatest.
A larger absolute value means a smaller number when both are negative.
−4 is to the left of −1/2, so it is less than −1/2.

hints.en: On a number line, numbers to the right are greater.
Among negative numbers, the one closest to 0 is greatest.
Which number is the least far below 0?

steps: Place −5, −4.5, −4 and −1/2 on a number line.
−1/2 is farthest to the right, so it is greatest.
solution.es: −1/2 está más a la derecha en la recta numérica, así que es el mayor.

objective: Use absolute value as a distance from 0 in a context.

stem.en: A hiker is at an elevation of −17 meters, which is below sea level. How many meters is she from sea level?
stem.es: Una excursionista está a una elevación de −17 metros, es decir, bajo el nivel del mar. ¿A cuántos metros está del nivel del mar?

hints.en: Distance is never negative.
Absolute value tells how far a number is from 0.
Remove the negative sign and keep the size.

solution.es: |−17| = 17: está a 17 metros del nivel del mar.

objective: Find the distance between two points that share a y-coordinate.

stem.en: A kite is at (−5, 2) and its anchor is at (3, 2). How many units is the kite from the anchor?
stem.es: Una cometa está en (−5, 2) y su ancla está en (3, 2). ¿A cuántas unidades está la cometa del ancla?

hints.en: The y-coordinates match, so the points are on a horizontal line.
Find the distance from each point to the y-axis.
They are on opposite sides of the y-axis, so add.

steps: The kite is 5 left of the y-axis and the anchor is 3 right.
solution.es: 5 a la izquierda y 3 a la derecha del eje y: 5 + 3 = 8 unidades.

objective: Find the least common multiple of two numbers.

stem.en: What is the least common multiple of 12 and 18?
stem.es: ¿Cuál es el mínimo común múltiplo de 12 y 18?

hints.en: List the first few multiples of each number.
Look for the first number that is in both lists.
Multiples of 18 are 18, 36, 54.

steps: The smallest multiple in both lists is 36.
solution.es: El primer múltiplo común de 12 y 18 es 36.

objective: Use the least common multiple to find when two repeating events coincide.

stem.en: Bus A leaves a stop every 8 minutes. Bus B leaves the same stop every 12 minutes. Both leave together at 7:00 a.m. How many minutes later do they next leave together?
stem.es: El autobús A sale de una parada cada 8 minutos. El autobús B sale de la misma parada cada 12 minutos. Ambos salen juntos a las 7:00 a.m. ¿Cuántos minutos después vuelven a salir juntos?

criteria.en: Lists multiples or uses LCM idea
criteria.es: Enumera múltiplos o usa la idea del mínimo común múltiplo

criteria.en: Finds 24 minutes
criteria.es: Halla 24 minutos

sample.en: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24. Multiples of 12: 12, 24. The least common multiple is 24, so they leave together again 24 minutes later.
sample.es: Múltiplos de 8: 8, 16, 24. Múltiplos de 12: 12, 24. El mínimo común múltiplo es 24, así que vuelven a salir juntos 24 minutos después.

hints.en: They leave together when the time is a multiple of both 8 and 12.
Write the multiples of each number until they match.
You want the first time they match, so it is the least common multiple.

solution.es: El primer múltiplo común de 8 y 12 es 24 minutos.

objective: Critique the claim that the LCM is always the product of two numbers.

stem.en: Sam says the least common multiple of 4 and 6 is 24, because 4 × 6 = 24. Is Sam right? Explain.
stem.es: Sam dice que el mínimo común múltiplo de 4 y 6 es 24, porque 4 × 6 = 24. ¿Tiene razón Sam? Explica.

criteria.en: Shows 12 is a multiple of both (12 ÷ 4 = 3 and 12 ÷ 6 = 2)
criteria.es: Muestra que 12 es múltiplo de ambos (12 ÷ 4 = 3 y 12 ÷ 6 = 2)

criteria.en: Notes 12 is smaller than 24, so 24 is not the least
criteria.es: Nota que 12 es menor que 24, así que 24 no es el mínimo

criteria.en: States the LCM is 12 and that 24 is only a common multiple
criteria.es: Indica que el mínimo común múltiplo es 12 y que 24 solo es un múltiplo común

sample.en: Sam is not right. 12 is also a multiple of 4 (4 × 3) and of 6 (6 × 2), and 12 is smaller than 24. So the LCM is 12. 24 is a common multiple but not the least one.
sample.es: Sam no tiene razón. 12 también es múltiplo de 4 (4 × 3) y de 6 (6 × 2), y 12 es menor que 24. Entonces el mínimo común múltiplo es 12. 24 es un múltiplo común pero no el menor.

hints.en: Look for a smaller number that both 4 and 6 divide into.
List the multiples of each number in order.
Check whether 12 works for both.

steps: 12 is the first number on both lists, so the LCM is 12.
solution.es: El primer múltiplo común de 4 y 6 es 12, no 24.

objective: Identify a number that is less than a given negative decimal.

stem.en: Which number is less than −2.5?
stem.es: ¿Cuál número es menor que −2.5?

choices.why: −2 is to the right of −2.5, so it is greater than −2.5.
−1/2 is much closer to 0, so it is greater than −2.5.
Every positive number is greater than every negative number.

hints.en: Numbers to the left on a number line are less.
Picture −2.5 on a number line.
Which choice is farther left than −2.5?

steps: Numbers less than −2.5 are to its left.
Only −3 is to the left of −2.5.
solution.es: Solo −3 está a la izquierda de −2.5, así que es menor.

objective: Use coordinates to solve a distance problem on a map.

stem.en: On a town map, each unit is one block. The library is at (−4, 3) and the school is at (−4, −5). If you walk straight along the street from the library to the school, how many blocks do you walk?
stem.es: En el mapa de un pueblo, cada unidad es una cuadra. La biblioteca está en (−4, 3) y la escuela está en (−4, −5). Si caminas en línea recta por la calle de la biblioteca a la escuela, ¿cuántas cuadras caminas?

criteria.en: Sees the points share x = −4, so the path is vertical
criteria.es: Ve que los puntos comparten x = −4, así que el camino es vertical

criteria.en: Adds 3 and 5 because they are on opposite sides of the x-axis to get 8
criteria.es: Suma 3 y 5 porque están en lados opuestos del eje x y obtiene 8

sample.en: Both points have x = −4, so I walk along a vertical line. The library is 3 above the x-axis and the school is 5 below it, so 3 + 5 = 8 blocks.
sample.es: Ambos puntos tienen x = −4, así que camino por una línea vertical. La biblioteca está 3 sobre el eje x y la escuela 5 bajo él, entonces 3 + 5 = 8 cuadras.

hints.en: Compare the x-coordinates of the two places.
Which coordinate changes along the walk?
3 above the axis and 5 below it are on opposite sides.

steps: Same x, so the walk is vertical.
solution.es: Misma x: camino vertical; 3 + 5 = 8 cuadras.

objective: Find where a zero was dropped in the quotient.

stem.en: Sam divides 7,208 ÷ 8. Step 1: 8 goes into 72 nine times, so write 9. Step 2: Bring down 0. 8 does not go into 0, so skip it and write nothing. Step 3: Bring down 8; 8 goes into 8 once, so write 1. Sam's answer is 91. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Sam divide 7,208 ÷ 8. Paso 1: 8 cabe en 72 nueve veces, así que escribe 9. Paso 2: Baja el 0. 8 no cabe en 0, así que lo salta y no escribe nada. Paso 3: Baja el 8; 8 cabe en 8 una vez, así que escribe 1. La respuesta de Sam es 91. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: 8 goes into 72 nine times, so write 9.
Bring down 0, skip it and write nothing.
Bring down 8; 8 goes into 8 once, so write 1.

hints.en: Check Sam's answer by multiplying 91 × 8.
Every digit you bring down needs a digit in the quotient.
8 goes into 0 zero times, and that zero must be written.

steps: Step 2 should write 0 in the quotient, so the answer is 901.
solution.es: Hay que escribir 0 en el cociente: 7,208 ÷ 8 = 901.

objective: Locate a negative decimal on a number line.

stem.en: The number line from −4 to 0 has a tick every half unit. Place a point at −2.5.
stem.es: La recta numérica de −4 a 0 tiene una marca cada media unidad. Coloca un punto en −2.5.

hints.en: −2.5 is halfway between two integers.
It is between −3 and −2.
Find the tick midway between those two integers.

solution.es: −2.5 está a la mitad entre −3 y −2.

stem.en: The number line from −1 to 1 is cut into fourths. Place a point at −3/4.
stem.es: La recta numérica de −1 a 1 está dividida en cuartos. Coloca un punto en −3/4.

hints.en: Negative numbers are to the left of 0.
Count fourths to the left, starting at 0.
Make 3 hops of size 1/4 to the left.

steps: Start at 0 and move left 3 fourths.

objective: Divide a fraction by a fraction to find the number of servings.

stem.en: A shop has 5/6 pound of nuts. Each small bag holds 2/3 pound. How many bags can be filled? Write the answer as a fraction.

Multiply 5/6 by the flipped version of the second fraction.

stem.en: A painter has 1/2 gallon of paint and pours it equally into 3 cans. How much paint is in each can?
stem.es: Un pintor tiene 1/2 galón de pintura y la vierte en partes iguales en 3 latas. ¿Cuánta pintura hay en cada lata?

objective: Solve a real-world division problem with a multi-digit dividend.

stem.en: A school orders 1,764 pencils. They come in boxes of 12. How many boxes does the school get?
stem.es: Una escuela pide 1,764 lápices. Vienen en cajas de 12. ¿Cuántas cajas recibe la escuela?

criteria.es: Escribe la división 1,764 ÷ 12

criteria.en: Gets 147 boxes
criteria.es: Obtiene 147 cajas

hints.en: Each box holds the same number of pencils.
Divide the total pencils by the pencils in one box.
Check by multiplying your answer by 12.

objective: Find the step where the coordinates of a point were read in the wrong order.

stem.en: Maya plots (−2, 4). Step 1: The first number is the x-coordinate and the second is the y-coordinate. Step 2: Start at the origin, move 4 units left, then 2 units up. Step 3: Mark the point. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Maya marca (−2, 4). Paso 1: El primer número es la coordenada x y el segundo es la coordenada y. Paso 2: Parte del origen, se mueve 4 unidades a la izquierda y luego 2 unidades hacia arriba. Paso 3: Marca el punto. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: The first number is the x-coordinate and the second is the y-coordinate.
Start at the origin, move 4 units left, then 2 units up.

hints.en: Compare what Step 2 does with what Step 1 says.
The x-coordinate tells the horizontal move.
The x-coordinate is −2, so the horizontal move is 2 units left.

steps: x = −2 means 2 units left, and y = 4 means 4 units up.
Step 2 swapped the numbers; the point is 2 left and 4 up.
solution.es: x = −2 es 2 a la izquierda y y = 4 es 4 hacia arriba; el paso 2 invirtió los números.

objective: Name the quadrant of a point from the signs of its coordinates.

stem.en: Point A is at (−4, 5). In which quadrant is Point A?
stem.es: El punto A está en (−4, 5). ¿En qué cuadrante está el punto A?

choices.why: Quadrant III needs both coordinates negative. The y-coordinate here is 5, which is positive.
Quadrant I needs both coordinates positive. The x-coordinate here is −4.
Quadrant IV has a positive x and a negative y. This point has the opposite signs.

hints.en: Look at the sign of each coordinate.
A negative x-coordinate puts the point left of the y-axis.
A positive y-coordinate puts it above the x-axis.

steps: x = −4 is negative (left) and y = 5 is positive (up).
Left and up is Quadrant II.
solution.es: x negativo y y positivo: cuadrante II.

verify.note: Quadrant naming follows from the signs of the coordinates; checked by inspection against the standard quadrant definitions.

objective: Identify points in Quadrant III from their coordinates.

stem.en: Select ALL the points that are in Quadrant III.
stem.es: Selecciona TODOS los puntos que están en el cuadrante III.

choices.why: The y-coordinate 2 is positive, so this point is in Quadrant II.
The x-coordinate 3 is positive, so this point is in Quadrant IV.

hints.en: Quadrant III is down and to the left of the origin.
Both coordinates must be negative.
Check the sign of x first, then the sign of y.

steps: (3, −4) is in Quadrant IV and (−6, 2) is in Quadrant II.
solution.es: El cuadrante III tiene ambas coordenadas negativas.

verify.note: Quadrant III is the set of points with both coordinates negative; each choice is classified by the signs of its coordinates.

objective: Locate a fraction quotient on a number line.

stem.en: Place a point on the number line at the value of 3/4 ÷ 1/2.
stem.es: Coloca un punto en la recta numérica en el valor de 3/4 ÷ 1/2.

hints.en: Ask how many halves fit in 3/4.
Dividing by 1/2 is the same as multiplying by 2.
3/4 × 2 is between 1 and 2.

steps: 6/4 = 1 1/2, which is the tick halfway between 1 and 2.
solution.es: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 6/4 = 1 1/2: el punto va a la mitad entre 1 y 2.

objective: Find the step where the wrong fraction was flipped.

stem.en: Lena solves 2/3 ÷ 1/4. Step 1: Flip the first fraction to get 3/2. Step 2: Multiply 3/2 × 1/4. Step 3: The answer is 3/8. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Lena resuelve 2/3 ÷ 1/4. Paso 1: Voltea la primera fracción y obtiene 3/2. Paso 2: Multiplica 3/2 × 1/4. Paso 3: La respuesta es 3/8. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: Flip the first fraction to get 3/2.

hints.en: Only one of the two fractions is replaced by its reciprocal.
Which fraction is the divisor?
Keep 2/3 the same and flip the divisor 1/4.

steps: The divisor is 1/4, so its reciprocal is 4.
solution.es: Se voltea el divisor 1/4, no el dividendo: 2/3 × 4 = 8/3.

objective: Find the coordinates of a reflection across an axis.

stem.en: The point (3, −5) is reflected across the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the new point?
stem.es: El punto (3, −5) se refleja sobre el eje x. ¿Cuál es la coordenada y del nuevo punto?

choices.why: That is the original y-coordinate. A reflection across the x-axis changes the sign of y.
The x-coordinate does not change, and −3 is not related to y.
3 is the x-coordinate, which stays the same.

hints.en: Reflecting across the x-axis flips the point over a horizontal line.
The point stays the same distance from the x-axis but ends up on the other side.
Only one coordinate changes sign.

steps: A reflection across the x-axis keeps x and changes the sign of y.
solution.es: Al reflejar sobre el eje x cambia el signo de y: (3, 5).

objective: Plot the reflection of a point across the y-axis.

stem.en: Point A is at (2, 3). Plot Point B, the reflection of A across the y-axis.
stem.es: El punto A está en (2, 3). Marca el punto B, la reflexión de A sobre el eje y.

hints.en: The y-axis is a vertical mirror.
B is the same distance from the y-axis but on the other side.
The height of the point does not change.

steps: A is 2 units right of the y-axis, so B is 2 units left: x = −2.
solution.es: B está a la misma distancia del eje y al otro lado: B = (−2, 3).

objective: Find how many equal fractional pieces fit in a fraction of a whole.

stem.en: A ribbon is 3/4 yard long. It is cut into pieces that are each 1/8 yard long. How many pieces are there?
stem.es: Una cinta mide 3/4 de yarda de largo. Se corta en pedazos que miden 1/8 de yarda cada uno. ¿Cuántos pedazos hay?

hints.en: Think: how many eighths fit in 3/4?
Write 3/4 as eighths.
3/4 is the same as 6/8, so count the eighths.

solution.es: 3/4 = 6/8, así que caben 6 pedazos de 1/8.

objective: Find a unit price by dividing decimals.

stem.en: A 2.5 kilogram bag of rice costs $6.75. What is the price for one kilogram?
stem.es: Una bolsa de arroz de 2.5 kilogramos cuesta $6.75. ¿Cuál es el precio de un kilogramo?

criteria.en: Divides the price by the number of kilograms
criteria.es: Divide el precio entre el número de kilogramos

criteria.en: Gets $2.70 per kilogram
criteria.es: Obtiene $2.70 por kilogramo

sample.en: 6.75 ÷ 2.5 = 67.5 ÷ 25 = 2.7. The rice costs $2.70 per kilogram.
sample.es: 6.75 ÷ 2.5 = 67.5 ÷ 25 = 2.7. El arroz cuesta $2.70 por kilogramo.

hints.en: Unit price is the cost of 1 kilogram.
Divide dollars by kilograms.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to make the divisor a whole number.

solution.es: 6.75 ÷ 2.5 = 2.7 dólares por kilogramo.

objective: Find a coordinate of a point at a given distance along a horizontal line.

stem.en: A point is on the same horizontal line as (2, −1) and 5 units to its left. What is the x-coordinate of the point?
stem.es: Un punto está en la misma línea horizontal que (2, −1) y a 5 unidades a su izquierda. ¿Cuál es la coordenada x del punto?

choices.why: −5 is the distance, not the position. Start from x = 2 and move left.
That subtracts the wrong way: 5 − 2. Start at 2 and move 5 to the left.
That moves 5 units to the right, not to the left.

hints.en: Moving left on a horizontal line makes x smaller.
The y-coordinate stays the same.
Start at x = 2 and take away 5.

steps: Moving 5 units left subtracts 5 from the x-coordinate.
solution.es: Moverse 5 unidades a la izquierda: 2 − 5 = −3.

objective: Choose the expression that models sharing a fraction equally.

stem.en: Four friends share 3/5 of a pizza equally. Which expression gives the amount each friend gets?
stem.es: Cuatro amigos se reparten 3/5 de una pizza en partes iguales. ¿Qué expresión da la cantidad que recibe cada amigo?

choices.why: Multiplying makes the amount bigger. Sharing gives each friend less than 3/5.
Sharing equally is division, not subtraction, and the result would be negative.
That asks how many 3/5-size pieces are in 4 wholes. Here the 3/5 is being shared, so it is divided by 4.

hints.en: Sharing equally means dividing.
What is being shared, and how many people share it?
The amount shared is the first number in the division.

steps: Total shared: 3/5 of a pizza. Number of friends: 4.
solution.es: Se reparte 3/5 entre 4: 3/5 ÷ 4 = 3/20.

objective: Match a fraction division expression to a real-world story.

stem.en: Which story matches 2 ÷ 1/4, and what is its answer?
stem.es: ¿Qué situación corresponde a 2 ÷ 1/4, y cuál es su respuesta?

text.en: What is 2 cups plus 1/4 cup? 2 1/4 cups
text.es: ¿Cuánto es 2 tazas más 1/4 de taza? 2 1/4 tazas

choices.why: That adds the amounts. The expression is a division.
Finding 1/4 of 2 is multiplication (1/4 × 2), not division.

text.en: How many 1/4-cup scoops are in 2 cups? 8 scoops
text.es: ¿Cuántas medidas de 1/4 de taza hay en 2 tazas? 8 medidas

text.en: How much does each of 4 friends get if they share 2 cups equally? 1/2 cup
text.es: ¿Cuánto recibe cada uno de 4 amigos si reparten 2 tazas por igual? 1/2 taza

choices.why: That shares 2 among 4, which is 2 ÷ 4. The story for 2 ÷ 1/4 asks how many fourths fit in 2.

hints.en: Dividing by 1/4 asks: how many fourths fit?
Count how many quarter-cups make 1 cup, then 2 cups.
There are 4 fourths in each whole.

solution.es: Cada taza tiene 4 cuartos, así que 2 ÷ 1/4 = 8.

objective: Plot an ordered pair with a negative coordinate described in words.

stem.en: A treasure is 3 units to the left of the y-axis and 2 units above the x-axis. Plot the treasure.
stem.es: Un tesoro está a 3 unidades a la izquierda del eje y y a 2 unidades sobre el eje x. Marca el tesoro.

hints.en: Left of the y-axis means a negative x-coordinate.
Above the x-axis means a positive y-coordinate.
Write the pair as (x, y) before plotting it.

steps: 3 units left gives x = −3; 2 units up gives y = 2.
solution.es: 3 a la izquierda es x = −3 y 2 hacia arriba es y = 2: el punto es (−3, 2).

objective: Evaluate repeated opposites of a number.

stem.en: Simplify the nested opposites: −(−(−8)).
stem.es: Simplifica los opuestos anidados: −(−(−8)).

hints.en: The opposite of a number is on the other side of 0.
Start with the innermost opposite: −(−8).
Each extra opposite flips the sign once.

objective: Use opposites to undo a change in a context.

stem.en: Mia's savings changed by −$45 on Monday. What change on Tuesday would bring her savings back to where they were before Monday?
stem.es: Los ahorros de Mia cambiaron −$45 el lunes. ¿Qué cambio el martes los devolvería a lo que eran antes del lunes?

hints.en: The change on Monday took money away.
To get back to the start you need the opposite change.
The opposite of a negative number is positive.

steps: A change of +$45 on Tuesday returns the savings to the start.
solution.es: El opuesto de −45 es 45: un cambio de +$45 restaura los ahorros.

objective: Find the distance between two points that share an x-coordinate.

stem.en: Point P is at (−3, 4) and Point Q is at (−3, −2). How many units apart are P and Q?
stem.es: El punto P está en (−3, 4) y el punto Q está en (−3, −2). ¿Cuántas unidades hay entre P y Q?

hints.en: The two points have the same x-coordinate, so they are on a vertical line.
Find how far each y-coordinate is from 0.
The points are on opposite sides of the x-axis, so add the distances.

steps: P is 4 above the x-axis and Q is 2 below it.
solution.es: P está 4 sobre el eje x y Q está 2 bajo él: 4 + 2 = 6 unidades.

objective: Sort situations by whether they are above, below or at the reference point of 0.

stem.en: Sort each situation by what it means compared with the starting point (0).
stem.es: Clasifica cada situación según lo que significa respecto al punto de partida (0).

items.en: A bird flying 30 feet above the ground
items.es: Un pájaro volando a 30 pies sobre el suelo

items.en: A parking level two floors underground
items.es: Un nivel de estacionamiento a dos pisos bajo tierra
Una temperatura 4 grados bajo el punto de congelación

items.en: A balloon exactly at ground level
items.es: Un globo justo al nivel del suelo

hints.en: Decide what the starting point 0 is in each situation.
Is the quantity higher than, lower than, or exactly at that starting point?
A balance of exactly nothing owed or saved sits at 0.

steps: Above the reference point means positive.
Below means negative, and exactly at the point means 0.
solution.es: Sobre el punto de referencia es positivo; bajo es negativo; justo en el punto es 0.

verify.note: Classification by meaning in context; the sort has no numeric computation to prove.

objective: Explain what zero means in a context and why it is neither positive nor negative.

stem.en: On a winter day, the thermometer reads 0 degrees Celsius. Explain what the 0 tells you and why it is neither a positive nor a negative temperature.
stem.es: En un día de invierno, el termómetro marca 0 grados Celsius. Explica qué te dice el 0 y por qué no es una temperatura positiva ni negativa.

criteria.en: States 0 is the dividing point between temperatures above and below freezing
criteria.es: Indica que 0 es el punto que separa las temperaturas sobre y bajo el punto de congelación

criteria.en: Says positive temperatures are above 0 and negative ones are below 0
criteria.es: Dice que las temperaturas positivas están sobre 0 y las negativas bajo 0

criteria.en: Concludes 0 is neither above nor below itself
criteria.es: Concluye que 0 no está ni sobre ni bajo sí mismo

sample.en: 0 degrees is the freezing point. Temperatures above it are positive and temperatures below it are negative. 0 is not above or below itself, so it is neither positive nor negative.
sample.es: 0 grados es el punto de congelación. Las temperaturas sobre él son positivas y las temperaturas bajo él son negativas. El 0 no está ni sobre ni bajo sí mismo, así que no es ni positivo ni negativo.

hints.en: Think about where 0 sits on a thermometer.
What kind of temperatures are above 0? Below 0?
Is 0 above 0? Is it below 0?

steps: Positive temperatures are above 0 and negative temperatures are below 0.
0 is the point between them, so it is neither.
solution.es: El 0 separa los números positivos de los negativos, por lo que no es ni positivo ni negativo.

verify.note: Explanation of the meaning of zero as a reference point; judged by rubric, not computation.

objective: Divide a three-digit number by a two-digit number.

stem.en: A teacher has 945 stickers to share equally among 15 classes. How many stickers does each class get?
stem.es: Una maestra tiene 945 calcomanías para repartir por igual entre 15 clases. ¿Cuántas calcomanías recibe cada clase?

hints.en: Equal sharing means dividing.
15 goes into 94 six times.
Multiply, subtract, bring down the next digit and divide again.

steps: 15 into 94 is 6 (90), remainder 4; bring down 5 to make 45.
15 into 45 is 3, so each class gets 63.
solution.es: 945 ÷ 15 = 63 calcomanías por clase.

objective: Divide a four-digit number by a two-digit number in a context and judge the result.

stem.en: A family drives 3,570 miles on a road trip. They drive the same distance each day for 15 days. How many miles do they drive each day?
stem.es: Una familia recorre 3,570 millas en un viaje por carretera. Recorren la misma distancia cada día durante 15 días. ¿Cuántas millas recorren cada día?

choices.why: 15 × 248 = 3,720, which is more than 3,570. Check by multiplying.
15 × 258 = 3,870, which is too large.
That has an extra digit. 15 × 2,380 is far more than 3,570.

hints.en: Divide the total distance by the number of days.
Estimate: 15 times 200 is 3,000.
Check by multiplying your quotient by 15.

steps: 15 × 238 = 3,570, so they drive 238 miles each day.
solution.es: 3,570 ÷ 15 = 238 millas por día.

objective: Add two decimals in a context.

stem.en: A runner jogged 12.5 kilometers on Saturday and 7.25 kilometers on Sunday. How many kilometers did she jog in all?
stem.es: Una corredora trotó 12.5 kilómetros el sábado y 7.25 kilómetros el domingo. ¿Cuántos kilómetros trotó en total?

hints.en: Line up the decimal points.
Write 12.5 as 12.50 so both numbers have two decimal places.
Add the hundredths, then tenths, then ones and tens.

objective: Order integers in a temperature context to find the least.

stem.en: Four towns reported morning temperatures in degrees Celsius. Which temperature is the coldest?
stem.es: Cuatro pueblos informaron temperaturas matutinas en grados Celsius. ¿Cuál temperatura es la más fría?

choices.why: −2 is warmer than −7. It is closer to 0.
0 is warmer than any negative temperature.
3 is above 0, so it is warmer than every negative temperature.

hints.en: Colder means farther down on a thermometer.
Negative numbers are below 0.
Among negative numbers, the one farthest from 0 is the least.

solution.es: −7 está más lejos de 0 hacia abajo, así que es la más fría.

objective: Divide a fraction by a fraction when the quotient is not a whole number.

stem.en: A pitcher has 2/5 liter of juice. Each cup takes 3/10 liter. How many cups can be filled? Give the exact amount as a fraction.
stem.es: Una jarra tiene 2/5 de litro de jugo. Cada vaso lleva 3/10 de litro. ¿Cuántos vasos se pueden llenar? Da la cantidad exacta como fracción.

hints.en: How many 3/10s fit in 2/5?
Write 2/5 as tenths to compare sizes.
Multiply 2/5 by the reciprocal of 3/10.

objective: Identify the least common multiple of two numbers from choices.

stem.en: Which number is the least common multiple of 6 and 15?
stem.es: ¿Qué número es el mínimo común múltiplo de 6 y 15?

choices.why: 3 is the greatest common factor, not the least common multiple.
60 is a common multiple, but 30 is smaller and also a multiple of both.
6 × 15 = 90 is a common multiple, but a smaller one also works.

hints.en: A common multiple is a multiple of both numbers.
List the multiples of 15 and check which are also multiples of 6.
The first one you find is the least.

steps: 30 is the first that 6 also divides into: 6 × 5 = 30.
solution.es: El primer múltiplo de 15 que también es múltiplo de 6 es 30.

objective: Compare two decimal rates in a multi-step problem.

stem.en: A car travels 28.5 miles on 1.5 gallons of gas. A truck travels 52.8 miles on 3.2 gallons. How many more miles per gallon does the car get than the truck?
stem.es: Un carro recorre 28.5 millas con 1.5 galones de gasolina. Una camioneta recorre 52.8 millas con 3.2 galones. ¿Cuántas millas más por galón rinde el carro que la camioneta?

criteria.en: Finds the car's rate is 19 miles per gallon
criteria.es: Halla que el rendimiento del carro es 19 millas por galón

criteria.en: Finds the truck's rate is 16.5 miles per gallon
criteria.es: Halla que el rendimiento de la camioneta es 16.5 millas por galón

criteria.en: Subtracts to get 2.5
criteria.es: Resta para obtener 2.5

sample.en: Car: 28.5 ÷ 1.5 = 19 miles per gallon. Truck: 52.8 ÷ 3.2 = 16.5 miles per gallon. 19 − 16.5 = 2.5 more miles per gallon.
sample.es: Carro: 28.5 ÷ 1.5 = 19 millas por galón. Camioneta: 52.8 ÷ 3.2 = 16.5 millas por galón. 19 − 16.5 = 2.5 millas más por galón.

hints.en: Find miles per gallon for each vehicle separately.
Multiply both numbers by 10 to make each divisor a whole number.
Subtract the truck's rate from the car's rate.

solution.es: 19 − 16.5 = 2.5 millas por galón más.

objective: Locate a negative decimal in the middle of a number line.

stem.en: Mark −1.5 on a number line that starts at −3 and ends at 0, with a tick for every half.
stem.es: Marca −1.5 en una recta numérica que empieza en −3 y termina en 0, con una marca por cada mitad.

hints.en: −1.5 is the same as −1 1/2.
It lies between −2 and −1.
Find the tick halfway between those integers.

steps: Mark the tick midway between them.
solution.es: −1.5 está a la mitad entre −2 y −1.

objective: Reason about when the opposite of a number is greater than the number.

stem.en: For which value of n is the opposite of n, written −n, greater than n itself?
stem.es: ¿Para qué valor de n el opuesto de n, escrito −n, es mayor que el propio n?

choices.why: The opposite of 5 is −5, which is less than 5.
The opposite of 2 is −2, which is less than 2.
The opposite of 0 is 0, so −n equals n and is not greater.

hints.en: Try each value: find −n and compare it with n.
For a positive n, the opposite is on the left of 0.
Only a number on the negative side of 0 has an opposite to its right.

steps: For 0, 2 and 5 the opposite is equal or smaller.
solution.es: Si n = −3, entonces −n = 3 y 3 > −3.

verify.note: Reasoning about opposites of negative, zero and positive numbers; each choice is tested by substituting into −n > n by hand.

objective: Locate the opposite of a rational number on a number line.

stem.en: The number line runs from −1 to 1 in steps of 1/4. Place a point at the opposite of −3/4.
stem.es: La recta numérica va de −1 a 1 en pasos de 1/4. Coloca un punto en el opuesto de −3/4.

hints.en: Opposites are the same distance from 0 on opposite sides.
−3/4 is 3 fourths to the left of 0.
Go 3 fourths to the right of 0.

steps: Mark the tick 3 fourths to the right of 0.
solution.es: El opuesto de −3/4 es 3/4, a 3 cuartos a la derecha de 0.

objective: Locate a percent as a fraction on a number line from 0 to 1.

stem.en: The number line from 0 to 1 is cut into 20 equal parts. Place a point at 35%.
stem.es: La recta numérica de 0 a 1 está dividida en 20 partes iguales. Coloca un punto en 35%.

hints.en: Percent means out of 100, so 35% is 35/100.
Simplify 35/100 to twentieths.
Count that many parts from 0.

solution.es: 35% = 35/100 = 7/20: el punto está a 7 partes de 0.

objective: Plot the reflection of a point across the x-axis.

stem.en: A boat sits at (3, −2) on a harbor map. Plot the point that is its mirror image over the x-axis.
stem.es: Un bote está en (3, −2) en el mapa de un puerto. Marca el punto que es su imagen en espejo sobre el eje x.

hints.en: The x-axis is a horizontal mirror.
The new point is the same distance from the x-axis, but on the other side.
The x-coordinate stays the same.

steps: The boat is 2 units below the x-axis, so its mirror image is 2 units above it.
solution.es: El bote está 2 unidades bajo el eje x, así que su imagen está 2 unidades arriba: (3, 2).

objective: Divide a whole number by a fraction to find the number of pieces.

stem.en: A rope 3 meters long is cut into pieces that are each 3/8 meter long. How many pieces are made?
stem.es: Una soga de 3 metros de largo se corta en pedazos de 3/8 de metro cada uno. ¿Cuántos pedazos se obtienen?

hints.en: How many pieces of size 3/8 fit in 3 wholes?
Each whole holds 8/3 of a piece.
Dividing by 3/8 is the same as multiplying by 8/3.

objective: Find the volume of a small prism with three fractional edge lengths.

stem.en: Jenna built a jewelry box that measures 3/4 foot by 1/2 foot by 1/2 foot. Find the cubic feet of space inside it.
stem.es: Jenna construyó una caja de joyas que mide 3/4 de pie por 1/2 pie por 1/2 pie. Halla los pies cúbicos de espacio que hay dentro.

hints.en: Volume is length times width times height.
Multiply the three numerators together.
Multiply the three denominators together.

objective: Find a unit rate when the quantities are fractions.

stem.en: A tortoise walks 3/4 mile in 1/2 hour. At that steady rate, how many miles does it walk in 1 hour?
stem.es: Una tortuga camina 3/4 de milla en 1/2 hora. A ese ritmo constante, ¿cuántas millas camina en 1 hora?

hints.en: A unit rate is the distance for 1 whole hour.
If it walks 3/4 mile in half an hour, what happens in the second half hour?
Divide the distance by the time: 3/4 ÷ 1/2.

solution.es: 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/4 × 2 = 3/2 millas por hora.

objective: Scale a ratio with fractional quantities to find the amount for one unit.

stem.en: A half batch of cookies uses 3/5 cup of sugar. How many cups of sugar does a whole batch use?
stem.es: Media tanda de galletas usa 3/5 de taza de azúcar. ¿Cuántas tazas de azúcar usa una tanda completa?

hints.en: A whole batch is twice as big as a half batch.
Double the amount of sugar.
Doubling 3/5 gives a fraction with a numerator of 6.

solution.es: 3/5 ÷ 1/2 = 6/5 tazas de azúcar.

objective: Solve a constant speed problem using a unit rate.

stem.en: A cyclist rides at a steady speed and covers 36 kilometers in 2 hours. How far does she ride in 5 hours at the same speed?
stem.es: Una ciclista va a una velocidad constante y recorre 36 kilómetros en 2 horas. ¿Qué distancia recorre en 5 horas a la misma velocidad?

criteria.en: Finds the speed 18 km per hour
criteria.es: Halla la velocidad de 18 km por hora

criteria.en: Multiplies by 5 hours to get 90 km
criteria.es: Multiplica por 5 horas y obtiene 90 km

sample.en: 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km per hour. 18 × 5 = 90 km.
sample.es: 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km por hora. 18 × 5 = 90 km.

hints.en: A steady speed is a constant unit rate.
Find the distance in one hour first.
Multiply that by the number of hours.

solution.es: 36 ÷ 2 = 18 km por hora; 18 × 5 = 90 km.

objective: Find a unit rate with a decimal quotient.

stem.en: A bakery uses 42 eggs to make 8 identical cakes. How many eggs does each cake use?
stem.es: Una panadería usa 42 huevos para hacer 8 pasteles iguales. ¿Cuántos huevos usa cada pastel?

hints.en: Share the eggs equally among the cakes.
The answer is not a whole number, so keep dividing past the ones place.
42 ÷ 8 is a little more than 5.

solution.es: 42 ÷ 8 = 5.25 huevos por pastel.

objective: Use a conversion ratio in a recipe problem.

stem.en: A soup recipe needs 3 quarts of broth. Your measuring cup holds 1 cup. There are 4 cups in 1 quart. How many cups of broth do you need to measure?
stem.es: Una receta de sopa necesita 3 cuartos de caldo. Tu taza medidora tiene capacidad de 1 taza. Hay 4 tazas en 1 cuarto. ¿Cuántas tazas de caldo necesitas medir?

criteria.en: Uses 4 cups for each quart
criteria.es: Usa 4 tazas por cada cuarto

criteria.en: Multiplies 3 × 4 to get 12 cups
criteria.es: Multiplica 3 × 4 y obtiene 12 tazas

sample.en: Each quart is 4 cups, so 3 quarts is 3 × 4 = 12 cups.
sample.es: Cada cuarto son 4 tazas, así que 3 cuartos son 3 × 4 = 12 tazas.

hints.en: The measuring cup is the smaller unit.
Each quart equals 4 cups.
Multiply: quarts times cups per quart.

solution.es: 3 cuartos × 4 tazas por cuarto = 12 tazas.

objective: Find a unit rate by dividing a total distance by an amount of fuel.

stem.en: A car travels 180 miles on 6 gallons of gas. How many miles does it travel per gallon?
stem.es: Un carro recorre 180 millas con 6 galones de gasolina. ¿Cuántas millas recorre por galón?

hints.en: A unit rate tells how much for ONE of something.
Share the miles equally among the gallons.
Divide the miles by the number of gallons.

steps: Miles per gallon means miles ÷ gallons.
solution.es: 180 ÷ 6 = 30 millas por galón.

objective: Recognize ratios that describe the same relationship as 6 to 8.

stem.en: A shelter has 6 cats for every 8 dogs. Select ALL the statements that describe the same ratio of cats to dogs.
stem.es: Un refugio tiene 6 gatos por cada 8 perros. Selecciona TODAS las afirmaciones que describen la misma razón de gatos a perros.

choices.why: 14 is all the animals. This compares cats to the whole shelter, not cats to dogs.
That reverses the order. The shelter has more dogs than cats.

hints.en: Equal ratios can be made by multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number.
Check that cats come first and dogs come second.
Simplify each one and compare it with 6 to 8.

steps: 12 to 16 and 9 to 12 also simplify to 3 to 4; the other two choices do not.
solution.es: Se simplifica cada razón: 3 a 4, 12 a 16 y 9 a 12 son iguales a 6 a 8.

objective: Compare two unit prices to find the better buy.

stem.en: Brand A sells 12 ounces of cereal for $3.00. Brand B sells 20 ounces for $4.40. What is the lowest price per ounce?
stem.es: La marca A vende 12 onzas de cereal por $3.00. La marca B vende 20 onzas por $4.40. ¿Cuál es el precio más bajo por onza?

text.en: Both brands cost the same per ounce
text.es: Las dos marcas cuestan lo mismo por onza

choices.why: The two unit prices are different, so they do not cost the same.
$3.00 ÷ 12 = $0.25 is Brand A's price. Brand B's price per ounce is lower.
Check the division: $4.40 ÷ 20 is not $0.23.

hints.en: Find the price of ONE ounce for each brand.
Divide each price by its number of ounces.
Compare the two answers: which one is less money?

steps: Brand B: 4.40 ÷ 20 = 0.22 dollars per ounce, the lower price.
solution.es: Marca A: $0.25 por onza. Marca B: $0.22 por onza, que es menor.

objective: Use a part-to-part ratio's quantities to find the whole.

stem.en: In a chess club, 12 students are in sixth grade and 15 are in seventh grade. How many students are in the club in all?
stem.es: En un club de ajedrez hay 12 estudiantes de sexto grado y 15 de séptimo. ¿Cuántos estudiantes hay en el club en total?

hints.en: The ratio 12 to 15 compares two groups that make up the club.
Put the two groups together.
Add the number from each grade.

steps: The club is the two groups together.
solution.es: Se suman los dos grupos: 12 + 15 = 27 estudiantes.

objective: Critique additive reasoning about equivalent ratios.

stem.en: Dani says the ratios 4 to 6 and 6 to 8 are equivalent because you add 2 to both numbers. Explain what is wrong with Dani's thinking.
stem.es: Dani dice que las razones 4 a 6 y 6 a 8 son equivalentes porque se suma 2 a ambos números. Explica qué está mal en el razonamiento de Dani.

criteria.en: Simplifies 4:6 to 2:3 and 6:8 to 3:4
criteria.es: Simplifica 4:6 a 2:3 y 6:8 a 3:4

criteria.en: States 2:3 and 3:4 are different, so the ratios are not equivalent
criteria.es: Indica que 2:3 y 3:4 son distintas, así que las razones no son equivalentes

criteria.en: Says equivalent ratios come from multiplying both numbers by the same number, not adding
criteria.es: Dice que las razones equivalentes se forman multiplicando ambos números por el mismo número, no sumando

sample.en: 4:6 simplifies to 2:3 but 6:8 simplifies to 3:4. They are different. Equivalent ratios come from multiplying or dividing both numbers by the same number, not from adding the same amount.
sample.es: 4:6 se simplifica a 2:3 pero 6:8 se simplifica a 3:4. Son diferentes. Las razones equivalentes se forman multiplicando o dividiendo ambos números por el mismo número, no sumando la misma cantidad.

hints.en: Simplify each ratio to lowest terms.
Compare the simplified ratios.
Think about what operation keeps a ratio the same.

steps: 2/3 is not equal to 3/4, so adding 2 changed the relationship.
solution.es: 4:6 = 2:3 y 6:8 = 3:4; no son iguales, así que sumar 2 cambió la relación.

objective: Sort ratios by whether they are equivalent to 3 to 4.

stem.en: Sort each ratio by whether it is equivalent to 3 to 4.
stem.es: Clasifica cada razón según si es equivalente a 3 a 4.

hints.en: Equivalent ratios simplify to the same lowest-terms ratio.
Divide both numbers by the same amount.
Check whether you get back to 3 to 4.

solution.es: 6 a 8, 15 a 20 y 27 a 36 se simplifican a 3 a 4; las otras no.

objective: Explain why the order of quantities matters in a ratio.

stem.en: A fruit bowl has 3 apples and 5 oranges. Zoe says the ratio of apples to oranges and the ratio of oranges to apples mean the same thing. Explain why she is not right.
stem.es: Un frutero tiene 3 manzanas y 5 naranjas. Zoe dice que la razón de manzanas a naranjas y la razón de naranjas a manzanas significan lo mismo. Explica por qué no tiene razón.

criteria.en: Says apples to oranges is 3 to 5
criteria.es: Dice que manzanas a naranjas es 3 a 5

criteria.en: Says oranges to apples is 5 to 3 and the quantities swap places
criteria.es: Dice que naranjas a manzanas es 5 a 3 y que las cantidades cambian de lugar

criteria.en: Connects the order to the meaning (which fruit there is more of)
criteria.es: Relaciona el orden con el significado (de qué fruta hay más)

sample.en: Apples to oranges is 3 to 5, which compares 3 apples with 5 oranges. Oranges to apples is 5 to 3. The numbers swap, so it tells a different story: there are more oranges than apples.
sample.es: Manzanas a naranjas es 3 a 5. Naranjas a manzanas es 5 a 3. Los números cambian de lugar, así que cuentan otra historia: hay más naranjas que manzanas.

hints.en: Write both ratios using the numbers 3 and 5.
Which number is first in each ratio?
Think about which fruit each number stands for.

steps: Oranges to apples: 5 to 3, a different comparison.
solution.es: 3 a 5 y 5 a 3 son comparaciones distintas porque el orden cambia lo que cada número representa.

objective: Use a unit rate to find a new total.

stem.en: A garden hose fills a 45-gallon tub in 9 minutes. At the same rate, how many gallons does it pour in 25 minutes?
stem.es: Una manguera de jardín llena una tina de 45 galones en 9 minutos. Al mismo ritmo, ¿cuántos galones echa en 25 minutos?

criteria.en: Finds the unit rate 5 gallons per minute
criteria.es: Halla la tasa unitaria de 5 galones por minuto

criteria.en: Multiplies 5 by 25 minutes to get 125
criteria.es: Multiplica 5 por 25 minutos y obtiene 125

sample.en: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 gallons per minute. 5 × 25 = 125 gallons.
sample.es: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 galones por minuto. 5 × 25 = 125 galones.

hints.en: First find how many gallons flow in ONE minute.
Divide the gallons by the minutes for the unit rate.
Then use the unit rate for the new amount of time.

solution.es: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 galones por minuto; 5 × 25 = 125 galones.

objective: Solve a percent-off problem about a sale price.

stem.en: A winter jacket costs $75. Today it is 40% off. How much do you pay for the jacket?
stem.es: Una chaqueta de invierno cuesta $75. Hoy tiene 40% de descuento. ¿Cuánto pagas por la chaqueta?

criteria.en: Finds 40% of 75 is 30
criteria.es: Halla que el 40% de 75 es 30

criteria.en: Subtracts 30 from 75 to get 45
criteria.es: Resta 30 de 75 y obtiene 45

sample.en: 40% of 75 is 0.40 × 75 = 30. The sale price is 75 − 30 = 45 dollars.
sample.es: El 40% de 75 es 0.40 × 75 = 30. El precio de oferta es 75 − 30 = 45 dólares.

hints.en: The discount is a percent of the original price.
Find 40% of $75 first.
The discount comes off the price, so subtract.

solution.es: El descuento es 30 y 75 − 30 = 45 dólares.

objective: Express a unit rate as a fraction of a unit.

stem.en: A camp pours 7 cups of juice evenly into 4 jugs. How many cups of juice are in each jug? Write your answer as a fraction.
stem.es: Un campamento vierte 7 tazas de jugo en partes iguales en 4 jarras. ¿Cuántas tazas de jugo hay en cada jarra? Escribe tu respuesta como fracción.

hints.en: Each jug gets an equal share of the juice.
Equal sharing is division: cups ÷ jugs.
Write the division as a fraction with the cups on top.

solution.es: 7 tazas entre 4 jarras es 7 ÷ 4 = 7/4 de taza por jarra.

objective: Write a part-to-part ratio in the order the question asks.

stem.en: A bag holds 7 red marbles and 4 blue marbles. What is the ratio of blue marbles to red marbles?
stem.es: Una bolsa tiene 7 canicas rojas y 4 canicas azules. ¿Cuál es la razón de canicas azules a canicas rojas?

choices.why: 11 is all the marbles. That compares blue to the whole bag, not blue to red.
7 − 4 = 3 tells how many more red marbles there are. A ratio compares the amounts, it does not subtract them.
That is red to blue. The word that comes first in the question comes first in the ratio.

hints.en: The question names blue first.
Write the blue amount first and the red amount second.
Use the order blue to red.

steps: Blue is first, so write the 4 blue marbles first.
Red is second, so the ratio is 4 to 7.
solution.es: Azul va primero: la razón es 4 a 7.

objective: Find the step where a unit rate was divided in the wrong order.

stem.en: Dev reads 24 pages in 8 minutes and wants pages per minute. Step 1: The rate is 24 pages in 8 minutes. Step 2: Divide 8 by 24, which gives 1/3. Step 3: Dev reads 1/3 page per minute. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Dev lee 24 páginas en 8 minutos y quiere las páginas por minuto. Paso 1: La tasa es 24 páginas en 8 minutos. Paso 2: Divide 8 entre 24, y da 1/3. Paso 3: Dev lee 1/3 de página por minuto. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: The rate is 24 pages in 8 minutes.

hints.en: Pages per minute means pages for ONE minute.
Which quantity should be divided by which?
The number of pages should be divided by the number of minutes.

steps: Pages per minute is pages ÷ minutes = 24 ÷ 8.
24 ÷ 8 = 3, so Dev reads 3 pages per minute; 1/3 is minutes per page.
solution.es: Páginas por minuto es 24 ÷ 8 = 3; 1/3 son minutos por página.

objective: Use equivalent ratios to find a missing quantity.

stem.en: A paint mix uses 3 cans of blue for every 5 cans of white. How many cans of blue go with 20 cans of white?
stem.es: Una mezcla de pintura usa 3 latas de azul por cada 5 latas de blanco. ¿Cuántas latas de azul van con 20 latas de blanco?

hints.en: Find how many times the white amount 5 fits into 20.
Multiply the blue amount by that same number.
20 is 4 groups of 5.

solution.es: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 mezclas, y 3 × 4 = 12 latas de azul.

objective: Classify ratios as part-to-part or part-to-whole.

stem.en: A fruit basket has 5 apples, 3 pears and 2 plums. Sort each ratio by what it compares.
stem.es: Una canasta de frutas tiene 5 manzanas, 3 peras y 2 ciruelas. Clasifica cada razón según lo que compara.

hints.en: A part-to-whole ratio uses the total as one of its two numbers.
The total number of fruit here is 10.
If the second word is 'all fruit', it compares a part to the whole.

steps: Two named fruits are compared: part to part.
A fruit compared with all the fruit is part to whole.
solution.es: Dos frutas distintas: parte a parte. Una fruta y toda la fruta: parte a total.

verify.note: Classification by meaning of the ratio language; no numeric computation to prove.

objective: Find the step where a part-to-whole ratio was written wrongly.

stem.en: A box has 9 pens: 6 black and 3 blue. Ravi wrote: Step 1: Black to blue is 6 to 3. Step 2: Blue to all pens is 3 to 6. Step 3: Black to all pens is 6 to 9. Which step has the mistake?
stem.es: Una caja tiene 9 bolígrafos: 6 negros y 3 azules. Ravi escribió: Paso 1: Negros a azules es 6 a 3. Paso 2: Azules a todos los bolígrafos es 3 a 6. Paso 3: Negros a todos los bolígrafos es 6 a 9. ¿Qué paso tiene el error?

steps: Blue to all pens is 3 to 6.
Black to all pens is 6 to 9.

hints.en: Check what number stands for 'all the pens'.
Add the black and blue pens to find the total.
Step 2 uses 6 as the total, but 6 is only the black pens.

steps: Blue to all pens should be 3 to 9, not 3 to 6.
solution.es: El total es 9, así que azules a todos es 3 a 9, no 3 a 6.

objective: Find a percent of a quantity as a rate per 100.

stem.en: A school library has 80 new books. 35% of them are science books. How many science books is that?
stem.es: Una biblioteca escolar tiene 80 libros nuevos. El 35% son libros de ciencias. ¿Cuántos libros de ciencias son?

hints.en: Percent means per 100.
35% is the same as 35/100 or 0.35.
Multiply the decimal form by 80.

objective: Find the whole when a part and its percent are known.

stem.en: Maya has saved $36, which is 45% of the amount she needs for a tablet. How much does the tablet cost?
stem.es: Maya ha ahorrado $36, que es el 45% de lo que necesita para una tableta. ¿Cuánto cuesta la tableta?

hints.en: $36 is only a part. The whole cost is 100%.
If 45% is $36, what does 1% equal, or what does 5% equal?
Divide the part by the percent written as a decimal.

steps: 45% of the cost is 36, so cost × 0.45 = 36.
solution.es: Costo × 0.45 = 36, entonces costo = 36 ÷ 0.45 = 80 dólares.

objective: Write a part-to-whole ratio from a picture-like description.

stem.en: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices. 3 slices have mushrooms and the rest are plain. What is the ratio of mushroom slices to all the slices?
stem.es: Una pizza se corta en 8 rebanadas iguales. 3 rebanadas tienen champiñones y las demás son sencillas. ¿Cuál es la razón de rebanadas con champiñones a todas las rebanadas?

choices.why: 5 is the number of plain slices. The question asks about ALL 8 slices.
That puts the whole first. The mushroom slices are named first.
5 is the plain slices. The question asks about the mushroom slices.

hints.en: The second quantity in the ratio is every slice, not just one kind.
Count all the slices in the pizza.
Mushroom slices go first, all slices go second.

steps: The ratio of mushroom slices to all slices is 3 to 8.
solution.es: Rebanadas con champiñones a todas: 3 a 8.

objective: Compare two rates by finding unit rates and justify the comparison.

stem.en: Printer A prints 84 pages in 7 minutes. Printer B prints 135 pages in 9 minutes. Which printer is faster, and by how many pages per minute? Show the unit rate for each printer.
stem.es: La impresora A imprime 84 páginas en 7 minutos. La impresora B imprime 135 páginas en 9 minutos. ¿Cuál impresora es más rápida y por cuántas páginas por minuto? Muestra la tasa unitaria de cada impresora.

criteria.en: Finds Printer A prints 12 pages per minute (84 ÷ 7)
criteria.es: Halla que la impresora A imprime 12 páginas por minuto (84 ÷ 7)

criteria.en: Finds Printer B prints 15 pages per minute (135 ÷ 9)
criteria.es: Halla que la impresora B imprime 15 páginas por minuto (135 ÷ 9)

criteria.en: Concludes Printer B is faster by 3 pages per minute
criteria.es: Concluye que la impresora B es más rápida por 3 páginas por minuto

sample.en: A: 84 ÷ 7 = 12 pages per minute. B: 135 ÷ 9 = 15 pages per minute. Printer B is faster by 15 − 12 = 3 pages per minute.
sample.es: A: 84 ÷ 7 = 12 páginas por minuto. B: 135 ÷ 9 = 15 páginas por minuto. La impresora B es más rápida por 15 − 12 = 3 páginas por minuto.

hints.en: Compare the printers at the same amount of time: one minute.
Find pages per minute for each printer.
Subtract the two unit rates to compare.

steps: Printer B: 135 ÷ 9 = 15 pages per minute, so B is faster by 3.
solution.es: A imprime 12 páginas por minuto y B imprime 15, así que B es más rápida por 3.

objective: Match rates to their unit rates.

stem.en: Match each rate to its unit rate.
stem.es: Relaciona cada tasa con su tasa unitaria.

hints.en: Each unit rate tells the amount for exactly 1 unit.
Divide the first number by the second.
For 1.5 hours, think about how many halves of an hour fit in the total.

solution.es: Se divide el primer número entre el segundo para hallar la cantidad por una unidad.

objective: Match a ratio description to an equivalent way of saying it.

stem.en: Match each situation to the ratio that says the same thing in simplest form.
stem.es: Relaciona cada situación con la razón que dice lo mismo en su forma más simple.

left.en: 10 red pens in a pack of 25 pens
left.es: 10 bolígrafos rojos en un paquete de 25

hints.en: Divide both numbers in a ratio by the same number to simplify it.
Find the biggest number that goes into both amounts.
Check which quantity the situation names first.

solution.es: Divide ambas cantidades entre el mismo número para simplificar cada razón.

objective: Convert measurements with a ratio of units.

stem.en: A jump rope is 6 yards long. There are 3 feet in each yard. How many feet long is the rope?
stem.es: Una cuerda de saltar mide 6 yardas de largo. Hay 3 pies en cada yarda. ¿Cuántos pies mide la cuerda?

hints.en: Each yard is 3 feet.
Feet are smaller than yards, so there will be more feet than yards.
Multiply the number of yards by the feet in one yard.

steps: Each of the 6 yards is 3 feet.
solution.es: 6 yardas × 3 pies = 18 pies.

objective: Plot pairs from a ratio relationship on the coordinate plane.

stem.en: A sports drink uses 1 scoop of powder for every 4 cups of water. Plot the ordered pairs (scoops, cups of water) for 2 scoops and for 3 scoops.
stem.es: Una bebida deportiva usa 1 cucharada de polvo por cada 4 tazas de agua. Marca los pares ordenados (cucharadas, tazas de agua) para 2 cucharadas y para 3 cucharadas.

hints.en: For every 1 scoop there are 4 cups of water.
Multiply the number of scoops by 4 to get the cups.
The first number in each pair is scoops, the second is cups.

solution.es: 2 cucharadas necesitan 8 tazas: (2, 8). 3 cucharadas necesitan 12 tazas: (3, 12).

objective: Complete a ratio table using a multiplicative relationship.

stem.en: A ratio table shows pairs of (minutes, pages): (4, 6), (6, 9) and (10, ?). What number goes in place of the question mark?
stem.es: Una tabla de razones muestra pares de (minutos, páginas): (4, 6), (6, 9) y (10, ?). ¿Qué número va en lugar del signo de interrogación?

choices.why: That adds 2 to the 10 because 4 → 6 adds 2. Ratio tables multiply, they do not add the same amount.
That just adds 4 to 10. Use the same multiplier as the other pairs.
That adds 6 to 10. The pages grow by a multiplier, not by adding.

hints.en: Look at how pages relate to minutes in the first pair.
Pages are 1.5 times the minutes.
Apply that same relationship to 10 minutes.

solution.es: Las páginas son 1.5 veces los minutos, así que 10 × 1.5 = 15.

objective: Use a tape diagram to show copies of a ratio.

stem.en: The ratio of pencils to erasers in a kit is 5 to 2. Use the tape diagram to show 6 copies of the ratio.
stem.es: La razón de lápices a borradores en un kit es 5 a 2. Usa el diagrama de cinta para mostrar 6 copias de la razón.

hints.en: Each copy has the same number of pencils and erasers.
Increase the number of copies until it reaches 6.
Use the scale control to set the number of copies.

solution.es: 6 copias de 5 lápices y 2 borradores dan 30 lápices y 12 borradores.

objective: Use a double number line or table to solve a ratio problem and show reasoning.

stem.en: A theater sells 3 tickets for $27. A club needs 11 tickets. Use a double number line or a ratio table to find the total cost. Show your work.
stem.es: Un teatro vende 3 boletos por $27. Un club necesita 11 boletos. Usa una doble recta numérica o una tabla de razones para hallar el costo total. Muestra tu trabajo.

criteria.en: Finds the cost of 1 ticket is $9
criteria.es: Halla que 1 boleto cuesta $9

criteria.en: Multiplies 9 × 11 to get $99
criteria.es: Multiplica 9 × 11 y obtiene $99

criteria.en: Shows a double number line or ratio table
criteria.es: Muestra una doble recta numérica o una tabla de razones

sample.en: Tickets 3 → $27, so 1 ticket → $9. 11 tickets cost 9 × 11 = $99.
sample.es: Boletos 3 → $27, entonces 1 boleto → $9. 11 boletos cuestan 9 × 11 = $99.

hints.en: Find what ONE ticket costs.
On a double number line, 3 tickets line up with $27.
Scale the one-ticket cost up to 11 tickets.

objective: Convert kilograms to grams using a conversion rate.

stem.en: A bag of flour has a mass of 3.5 kilograms. There are 1,000 grams in 1 kilogram. How many grams is the bag?
stem.es: Una bolsa de harina tiene una masa de 3.5 kilogramos. Hay 1,000 gramos en 1 kilogramo. ¿Cuántos gramos tiene la bolsa?

hints.en: Grams are smaller than kilograms, so there will be more grams.
Each kilogram is 1,000 grams.
Multiply the kilograms by 1,000.

steps: Moving the decimal point 3 places right gives 3,500 grams.

objective: Use a percent bar to find a percent of a quantity.

stem.en: The bar stands for 120 students. Set the bar to 45% to find how many students that is.
stem.es: La barra representa 120 estudiantes. Ajusta la barra a 45% para hallar cuántos estudiantes son.

hints.en: The whole bar is 100%, and it stands for 120 students.
Use the control that sets a chosen percent.
Read the amount that matches 45% of the bar.

solution.es: 45% de 120 = 0.45 × 120 = 54 estudiantes.

objective: Combine a ratio with a unit conversion to solve a multi-step problem.

stem.en: A punch is made from juice and soda in the ratio 3 to 5. There are 16 cups in 1 gallon. How many cups of soda are needed to make 4 gallons of punch?
stem.es: Un ponche se hace con jugo y refresco en la razón 3 a 5. Hay 16 tazas en 1 galón. ¿Cuántas tazas de refresco se necesitan para hacer 4 galones de ponche?

criteria.en: Converts 4 gallons to 64 cups
criteria.es: Convierte 4 galones a 64 tazas

criteria.en: Finds the soda is 5 of every 8 parts
criteria.es: Halla que el refresco es 5 de cada 8 partes

criteria.en: Finds 5/8 of 64 is 40 cups
criteria.es: Halla que 5/8 de 64 es 40 tazas

sample.en: 4 gallons = 4 × 16 = 64 cups. Each batch has 3 + 5 = 8 parts, and 64 ÷ 8 = 8 cups per part. Soda is 5 parts: 5 × 8 = 40 cups.
sample.es: 4 galones = 4 × 16 = 64 tazas. Cada tanda tiene 3 + 5 = 8 partes, y 64 ÷ 8 = 8 tazas por parte. El refresco son 5 partes: 5 × 8 = 40 tazas.

hints.en: Change the gallons to cups first.
The whole punch is 3 + 5 = 8 equal parts.
Find the size of one part, then take 5 parts for the soda.

steps: Total cups = 4 × 16 = 64; each of the 8 parts is 8 cups.
solution.es: 64 tazas en total; cada parte tiene 8 tazas; el refresco son 5 partes: 40 tazas.

objective: Identify rates that have the same unit rate.

stem.en: Select ALL the descriptions that show a speed of 12 miles per hour.
stem.es: Selecciona TODAS las descripciones que muestran una rapidez de 12 millas por hora.

choices.why: 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 miles per hour, which is a little more than 12.
50 ÷ 5 = 10 miles per hour, not 12.

hints.en: Find the miles for ONE hour in each description.
Divide the miles by the hours.
Compare each result with 12.

solution.es: 36 ÷ 3, 6 ÷ 0.5 y 60 ÷ 5 dan 12 millas por hora.

objective: Choose the unit rate that matches a rate statement.

stem.en: A runner covers 12 kilometers in 3 hours. What is the unit rate in kilometers per hour?
stem.es: Un corredor recorre 12 kilómetros en 3 horas. ¿Cuál es la tasa unitaria en kilómetros por hora?

choices.why: That is hours per kilometer. The question asks for kilometers per hour.
That subtracts 12 − 3. A rate comes from dividing.
That multiplies 12 × 3. Divide the distance by the time.

hints.en: Kilometers per hour means kilometers for ONE hour.
Divide the distance by the time.
Which division gives kilometers for each hour?

solution.es: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 kilómetros por hora.

objective: Find a sale price after a percent discount.

stem.en: A $40 shirt is 25% off. What is the sale price?
stem.es: Una camisa de $40 tiene 25% de descuento. ¿Cuál es el precio de oferta?

choices.why: $10 is only the discount. The sale price is what is left after taking it off.
That adds the discount instead of subtracting it.
That divides by 0.25. Finding a percent of a number means multiplying.

hints.en: Find the discount amount first.
25% of $40 is a quarter of $40.
Take the discount away from the original price.

objective: Explain how two distributions with the same center can differ in spread.

stem.en: Class A scored 78, 80, 80 and 82 on a quiz. Class B scored 60, 75, 85 and 100. Show that both classes have the same mean, then explain how their score distributions differ.
stem.es: La clase A obtuvo 78, 80, 80 y 82 en un examen. La clase B obtuvo 60, 75, 85 y 100. Muestra que ambas clases tienen la misma media y luego explica en qué se diferencian sus distribuciones de puntajes.

criteria.en: Shows both means are 80
criteria.es: Muestra que ambas medias son 80

criteria.en: Finds the ranges are 4 and 40
criteria.es: Halla que los rangos son 4 y 40

criteria.en: Says Class A scores are clustered and Class B scores are spread out
criteria.es: Dice que los puntajes de la clase A están agrupados y los de la B están dispersos

sample.en: Class A: (78 + 80 + 80 + 82) ÷ 4 = 80. Class B: (60 + 75 + 85 + 100) ÷ 4 = 80. The means match. The range of Class A is 82 − 78 = 4 and of Class B is 100 − 60 = 40, so Class A's scores are close together and Class B's are far apart.
sample.es: Clase A: (78 + 80 + 80 + 82) ÷ 4 = 80. Clase B: (60 + 75 + 85 + 100) ÷ 4 = 80. Las medias son iguales. El rango de la clase A es 82 − 78 = 4 y el de la B es 100 − 60 = 40, así que los puntajes de A están cerca y los de B están lejos.

hints.en: Add the four scores in each class and divide by 4.
Find the range of each class.
Compare how close together the scores are.

objective: Compare two data sets using center and spread in context.

stem.en: Ana scored 8, 10, 12, 10 and 10 points in five games. Ben scored 2, 6, 10, 14 and 18 points. Use the mean and the range to explain who is the more consistent scorer.
stem.es: Ana anotó 8, 10, 12, 10 y 10 puntos en cinco juegos. Ben anotó 2, 6, 10, 14 y 18 puntos. Usa la media y el rango para explicar quién es el anotador más constante.

criteria.en: Finds both means are 10
criteria.es: Halla que ambas medias son 10

criteria.en: Finds the ranges are 4 for Ana and 16 for Ben
criteria.es: Halla que los rangos son 4 para Ana y 16 para Ben

criteria.en: Concludes Ana is more consistent because her scores are closer together
criteria.es: Concluye que Ana es más constante porque sus puntajes están más cerca

sample.en: Ana's mean is (8 + 10 + 12 + 10 + 10) ÷ 5 = 10 and Ben's mean is (2 + 6 + 10 + 14 + 18) ÷ 5 = 10. Ana's range is 12 − 8 = 4 and Ben's is 18 − 2 = 16. Ana is more consistent because her scores vary much less.
sample.es: La media de Ana es (8 + 10 + 12 + 10 + 10) ÷ 5 = 10 y la de Ben es (2 + 6 + 10 + 14 + 18) ÷ 5 = 10. El rango de Ana es 12 − 8 = 4 y el de Ben es 18 − 2 = 16. Ana es más constante porque sus puntajes varían mucho menos.

hints.en: Find the mean for each player.
Find the range for each player.
A smaller range means scores that are closer together.

steps: Ranges 4 and 16 show Ana's scores are much closer together.
solution.es: Las dos medias son 10, pero el rango de Ana (4) es menor que el de Ben (16), así que Ana es más constante.

objective: Report the number of observations in a data set shown as a frequency list.

stem.en: A dot plot of the number of goals scored per game has 2 dots at 1, 4 dots at 2, 3 dots at 3 and 1 dot at 4. How many games are in the data set?
stem.es: Un diagrama de puntos de los goles anotados por partido tiene 2 puntos en 1, 4 puntos en 2, 3 puntos en 3 y 1 punto en 4. ¿Cuántos partidos hay en el conjunto de datos?

hints.en: Each dot stands for one game.
Do not add the values 1, 2, 3 and 4.
Count all the dots.

solution.es: 2 + 4 + 3 + 1 = 10 partidos.

objective: Find the median of a data set with an even number of values in context.

stem.en: A bakery counted how many loaves it sold on eight days: 12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 17, 11 and 16. What is the median number of loaves sold?
stem.es: Una panadería contó cuántas barras vendió en ocho días: 12, 15, 9, 20, 14, 17, 11 y 16. ¿Cuál es la mediana del número de barras vendidas?

criteria.en: Averages the two middle values 14 and 15 to get 14.5
criteria.es: Promedia los dos valores del medio, 14 y 15, y obtiene 14.5

sample.en: Ordered: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20. With 8 values the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th: (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5 loaves.
sample.es: Ordenados: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16, 17, 20. Con 8 valores, la mediana es el promedio del 4.º y 5.º: (14 + 15) ÷ 2 = 14.5 barras.

hints.en: Put the numbers in order from least to greatest first.
With an even number of values there are two middle values.
The median is halfway between those two values.

steps: Ordered data have middle values 14 and 15.
solution.es: Los valores del medio son 14 y 15, y su promedio es 14.5.

objective: Choose the measure of center that best represents typical data with an outlier.

stem.en: Five houses on a street sold for $180,000, $190,000, $200,000, $210,000 and $2,000,000. Which statement best describes a typical sale price on this street?
stem.es: Cinco casas de una calle se vendieron por $180,000, $190,000, $200,000, $210,000 y $2,000,000. ¿Qué afirmación describe mejor un precio de venta típico en esta calle?

text.en: The maximum, $2,000,000, because it is the biggest sale
text.es: El máximo, $2,000,000, porque es la venta mayor

choices.why: The largest value is the least typical here.

text.en: The range, $1,820,000, because it is the largest number
text.es: El rango, $1,820,000, porque es el número mayor

choices.why: The range measures spread, not a typical value.

text.en: The median, $200,000, because the $2,000,000 sale does not pull it up
text.es: La mediana, $200,000, porque la venta de $2,000,000 no la sube

text.en: The mean, $556,000, because it uses every sale
text.es: La media, $556,000, porque usa todas las ventas

choices.why: The mean is pulled far above four of the five prices by one very large value, so it does not look typical.

hints.en: Find the mean and the median of the five prices.
Four prices are close together and one is very different.
Which measure stays near the four similar prices?

steps: The median is near the typical sale, while the mean is pulled up by $2,000,000.
solution.es: La mediana ($200,000) representa mejor el precio típico porque el valor extremo no la afecta.
